title: Number of Flowers in Full Bloom
statement:
Each pair `flowers[i] = [start, end]` says that flower `i` is fully open at every time from `start` through `end`, with both endpoints included. Person `i` shows up at time `people[i]`.

Return an array with one entry per person, in the same order as `people`, where entry `i` is how many flowers are fully open at the moment person `i` shows up.
notes:
## Intuition

The direct approach checks every flower for every person, which is O(n·m) and far too slow at 5·10^4 each. Instead, notice that at time `t` the open flowers are exactly those that have already started (start ≤ t) minus those that have already finished (end < t). Both counts are "how many values in a sorted list are below a limit", which binary search answers in O(log n).

## Approach

1. Copy the start times into `starts` and the end times into `ends`, and sort each list on its own.
2. `countBelow(sorted, limit)` binary searches for the first index whose value is not below `limit`; that index is how many values are strictly smaller.
3. For each arrival `time`, `started` is the number of starts below `time + 1` (start ≤ time).
4. `ended` is the number of ends below `time` (end < time), so flowers ending exactly at `time` still count.
5. Push `started - ended` and return `answer` in the original order of `people`.

## Example 1, step by step

`starts = [1, 3, 4, 9]`, `ends = [6, 7, 12, 13]`.

- `time = 2`: 1 start is ≤ 2, no end is < 2, so `1`.
- `time = 3`: starts 1 and 3 count, no end is < 3, so `2`.
- `time = 7`: starts 1, 3, 4 count, end 6 is < 7, so `3 - 1 = 2`.
- `time = 11`: all 4 starts count, ends 6 and 7 are < 11, so `4 - 2 = 2`.

The answer is `[1, 2, 2, 2]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O((n + m) log n): two sorts of n values, then two binary searches per person.
- Space: O(n) for the two sorted lists (plus the m answers).

## Pitfalls

- Mixing up the inclusive ends: a flower is still open at `end`, so subtract only ends strictly below `time`.
- Sorting the pairs by start and searching ends in that order does not work; the end times must be sorted separately.
- Sorting `people` to sweep is fine, but then the answers must be put back in arrival order.
- Default `sort()` compares as strings; always pass `(a, b) => a - b`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `starts` | all start times, sorted |
| `ends` | all end times, sorted |
| `countBelow` | number of values in a sorted list that are below `limit` |
| `left`, `right`, `mid` | the binary search window and its middle |
| `time` | the current person's arrival time |
| `started`, `ended` | flowers that have opened by `time` / closed before `time` |
| `answer` | the counts, one per person |

narration.3: Do the same with the end times, sorted independently of the starts.
narration.5: countBelow returns how many values in a sorted list are strictly smaller than limit.
narration.8: Shrink the window [left, right) until it pins down the first value that is not below limit.
narration.10: The middle value is still below limit, so the boundary lies to its right.
narration.11: Skip past mid and everything before it.
narration.13: Otherwise mid could be the boundary itself, so keep it in the window.
narration.16: left is now the index of the first value >= limit, which equals the count of smaller values.
narration.20: Answer each person in their original order.
narration.21: Flowers with start <= time have opened by now: count starts below time + 1.
narration.22: Flowers with end < time have already closed; one ending exactly at time is still open.
narration.23: Open flowers are those that started minus those that already ended.
